title: Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation
title_zh: 代码负责模拟，Jev 负责评估

paragraphs.en: Judgment models such as Jev return, in a single call and without reasoning text, a probability for each described option. This makes them attractive as an agent’s action-selection layer, but it is unclear which decisions they can be trusted with. We test Jev on reflection tests, one-shot matrix games, the text game ALFWorld and robot control, and find a sharp boundary. Jev succeeds when the right option can be judged from what the input describes, which we call evaluation . Specifically, it solves 99% of the counterintuitive Cognitive Reflection Test questions. However, it fails when the right option depends on simulation (i.e., predicting something not in the input), such as the opponent’s action or the subgoal that must come first. In games, Jev plays suboptimally as if its rational opponent acted at random, because the opponent’s action is not given. In ALFWorld, Jev favors commands that mention an object or place named in the task description. For example, given the task “put a clean knife in the drawer”, Jev carries an unwashed knife straight to the drawer instead of first washing it at the sink. Surprisingly, many of these failures are not due to a lack of knowledge. Asked separately what the opponent will do, Jev usually answers correctly, and it responds well given the opponent’s action. It fails when one call must both perform the simulation and evaluate based on it. This suggests letting code make the prediction or simulation. When code supplies it, such as a lookahead in ALFWorld and physics simulation in robot control, Jev becomes an expert controller through its general evaluation ability.
paragraphs.zh: 像 Jev 这样的判断模型，在一次调用中无需推理文本，即可为每个描述的选项返回一个概率值。 这使得它们适合作为智能体的动作选择层，但尚不清楚哪些决策可以委托给它们。 我们在反思测试、单次矩阵游戏、文本游戏 ALFWorld 和机器人控制中测试了 Jev，并发现了一个明显的界限。 当正确选项能从输入描述中判断出来时，Jev 就能成功，我们称之为“评估”。 具体来说，它能解决 99% 的反直觉认知反思测试问题。 然而，当正确选项依赖于模拟（即预测输入中未包含的内容），例如对手的动作或必须优先达成的子目标时，它便会失败。 在游戏场景中，Jev 的表现次优，仿佛其理性对手是随机行动的，因为对手的动作并未被提供。 在 ALFWorld 中，Jev 倾向于选择任务描述中提及了某个物体或地点的命令。 例如，面对“将一把干净的刀放入抽屉”的任务，Jev 会直接拿着一把未清洗的刀走向抽屉，而不是先在水槽里清洗它。 令人惊讶的是，这些失败中的许多并非由于知识不足所致。 当被单独询问对手会做什么时，Jev 通常能正确回答，并且在给定对手动作的情况下也能做出良好反应。 当一次调用必须同时执行模拟并基于该模拟进行评估时，它便会失败。 这表明应让代码本身来完成预测或模拟。 当代码提供这些信息时——例如 ALFWorld 中的前瞻计算和机器人控制中的物理模拟——Jev 便能凭借其通用的评估能力成为专业的控制器。

paragraphs.en: Many decisions of an agent are choices within a short list of options: the next command in a text game, the next move in a game or the next skill of a robot. Judgment models such as Jev, built as a general “System One”, target exactly this kind of choice ( TypeSafe, 2026 ) . In a single call and without reasoning text, Jev returns a probability for each described option. It needs no task-specific training and no output parsing. This makes Jev attractive as an agent’s action-selection layer, called at every step as a fast policy over listed actions.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体的许多决策都是在有限的选项列表中做出选择：例如文字游戏中的下一个指令、游戏中的下一步棋，或机器人的下一个技能。 像 Jev 这样的判断模型被构建为一种通用的“系统一”，其目标正是这类选择（TypeSafe, 2026）。 Jev 在一次调用中无需推理文本，即可为每个已描述的选项返回一个概率值。 它不需要针对特定任务进行训练，也不需要解析输出。 这使得 Jev 适合作为智能体的动作选择层，在每个步骤中被调用，作为已列出动作的快速策略。

paragraphs.en: But it is unclear which kind of decisions such a model can be trusted with. Benchmark scores do not provide the answer. For example, Jev alone solves 31% of ALFWorld games, but this number says how often it fails, not at which decisions. Two common views of such models do not provide the answer either. The first view comes from the “System One” label in the dual-process theory of Kahneman (2011) and Evans and Stanovich (2013) , which predicts failure wherever an intuitive option is wrong. Yet Jev solves 99% of Cognitive Reflection Test questions, which are built around an intuitive but wrong answer ( Frederick, 2005 ; Hagendorff et al., 2023 ) . The second view holds that small models lack reasoning. Yet when asked to predict the opponent’s action in a matrix game, Jev is usually right.
paragraphs.zh: 但尚不清楚这样的模型可以信任哪些类型的决策。 基准测试分数无法提供答案。 例如，Jev 单独就能解决 ALFWorld 游戏中 31% 的关卡，但这个数字反映的是它失败的比例，而非具体在哪些决策上出错。 关于这类模型的两种常见观点同样无法提供答案。 第一种观点源于卡尼曼（2011）以及埃文斯和斯坦诺维奇（2013）提出的双过程理论中的“系统一”概念，该理论预测，任何依赖直觉而错误的选择都会导致失败。 然而，Jev 能够解决认知反射测试中 99% 的问题，而这些问题的设计正是围绕一个直观但错误的答案展开的（Frederick, 2005；Hagendorff 等，2023）。 第二种观点认为，小型模型缺乏推理能力。 然而，当被要求在矩阵博弈中预测对手的行动时，Jev 通常能做出正确判断。

paragraphs.en: We test Jev on reflection tests, one-shot matrix games, the text game ALFWorld ( Shridhar et al., 2021 ) and robot control, and find a sharp boundary. Specifically, we find that Jev succeeds when the right option can be judged from what the input describes, which we call evaluation . For example, in a CRT question, a bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total, and the bat costs $1.00 more. By checking the listed prices against the question, Jev selects $0.05 for the ball and avoids the intuitive $0.10. However, Jev fails when the right option depends on simulation (i.e., predicting something not in the input), such as the opponent’s action or the subgoal that must come first. In RL terms, Jev behaves like a policy without a world model. It scores actions by the current input and does not look ahead.

paragraphs.en: This leads us to let code make the prediction or simulation. When code supplies it, Jev becomes an expert controller through its general evaluation ability. In one-shot games, stating the opponent’s action raises accuracy from 33% to 98% when the action with the highest average payoff is not the best action against a rational opponent. Even when the opponent’s action is not supplied, Jev can predict it in one call. Given this prediction in a second call, Jev plays the best action in 94% of cases. Similarly, with a lookahead in a copy of ALFWorld, solved games rise from 31% to 87% (Figure 1 , bottom right). Finally, in robot control, Jev never picks up a box when it chooses raw torques. In contrast, with skills for which code simulates the physical dynamics, it matches a hand-written controller on the native task and further generalizes to new task variants (22 of 40 episodes against 3).

sents.en: Similarly, with a lookahead in a copy of ALFWorld, solved games rise from 31% to 87% (Figure 1 , bottom right).
sents.zh: 同样地，通过在 ALFWorld 的副本中进行前瞻，成功解决的博弈比例从 31% 提升至 87%（图 1，右下角）。

sents.en: Finally, in robot control, Jev never picks up a box when it chooses raw torques.
sents.zh: 最后，在机器人控制中，当选择原始扭矩时，Jev 绝不会拿起箱子。

sents.en: In contrast, with skills for which code simulates the physical dynamics, it matches a hand-written controller on the native task and further generalizes to new task variants (22 of 40 episodes against 3).
sents.zh: 相比之下，对于代码能够模拟物理动态的技能，它在原生任务上的表现与手写控制器相当，并能进一步泛化到新的任务变体（40 轮中有 22 轮成功，而手写控制器仅成功 3 轮）。

paragraphs.en: This section defines evaluation and simulation and explains how we label each decision.
paragraphs.zh: 本节定义了评估与模拟，并说明了我们对每个决策进行标注的方法。

paragraphs.en: Setting. Jev (version jev-1.13.0 ) takes a JSON state and a list of candidate options, each with a text description ( TypeSafe, 2026 ) . It returns the chosen option, a probability for every option and a confidence, but no reasoning text. We use it zero-shot, with one fixed instruction per condition (Appendix A ). A decision is a triple ( x , A , a ⋆ ) (x,A,a^{\star}) , where x x is the state, A A the set of described candidate options and a ⋆ ⊆ A a^{\star}\subseteq A the correct ones.
paragraphs.zh: 设定。 Jev（版本 jev-1.13.0）接收一个 JSON 状态和一系列候选选项，每个选项都带有文本描述（TypeSafe, 2026）。 它返回所选的选项、每个选项的概率以及置信度，但不提供推理文本。 我们以零样本方式使用它，每个条件对应一条固定的指令（附录 A）。 一个决策是一个三元组 (x, A, a⋆) (x,A,a^{\star})，其中 x 是状态，A 是已描述的候选选项集合，而 a⋆ ⊆ A 是正确的选项。

paragraphs.en: A decision needs only evaluation if a ⋆ a^{\star} can be judged from what x x and the candidate options describe. On the other hand, a decision depends on simulation if finding a ⋆ a^{\star} requires a prediction z z with information not in the input. The prediction can be shared by all candidate options, like the opponent’s action or the next subgoal. It can also belong to one candidate option, like the observation that follows it. If code supplies z z by adding it to x x , the decision needs only evaluation. Code can obtain z z by running a simulator, such as the game rules, a copy of the environment or a physics engine, or by asking the model in a separate call.
paragraphs.zh: 如果可以从 x x 和候选选项的描述中判断出 ⋆ a^{\star}，那么决策只需评估即可。 另一方面，如果找到 ⋆ a^{\star} 需要借助一个预测 z z，而该预测包含输入中不存在的信息，那么决策就依赖于模拟。 所有候选选项都可以共享这个预测，例如对手的行动或下一个子目标。 它也可能属于某个特定的候选选项，例如紧随其后的观察结果。 如果代码通过将其添加到 x x 中来提供 z z，那么决策只需评估即可。 代码可以通过运行模拟器（例如游戏规则、环境的副本或物理引擎）来获取 z z，也可以通过单独调用模型来获得。

paragraphs.en: Example 1 (one decision, presented two ways). When the agent holds an unwashed butterknife, going to the sink is right because the knife can be cleaned there. If an option only names a command, such as “go to sinkbasin 1”, the fact that the knife can be cleaned there must be simulated by code or predicted by the model (Figure 1 a). If an option also shows what the command makes possible, such as “Then: clean butterknife 2 with sinkbasin 1”, the same decision needs only evaluation (Figure 1 b).
paragraphs.zh: 示例 1（一个决策，以两种方式呈现）。 当智能体手持一把未清洗的餐刀时，前往水槽是正确的选择，因为可以在那里清洗这把刀。 如果某个选项仅命名了一个命令，例如“前往水槽盆 1”，那么必须通过代码模拟或模型预测来体现该处可以清洗餐刀这一事实（图 1 a）。 如果某个选项还展示了该命令能实现什么，例如“然后：用水槽盆 1 清洗餐刀 2”，那么同样的决策只需进行评估即可（图 1 b）。

sents.en: Example 1 (one decision, presented two ways).
sents.zh: 示例 1（一个决策，以两种方式呈现）。

sents.en: When the agent holds an unwashed butterknife, going to the sink is right because the knife can be cleaned there.
sents.zh: 当智能体手持一把未清洗的餐刀时，前往水槽是正确的选择，因为可以在那里清洗这把刀。

paragraphs.en: Knowing that a decision depends on simulation, however, does not separate real success from a lucky guess. A model can get such a decision right when a surface shortcut happens to point to the correct candidate option. Consider the task “put a clean butterknife in drawer”. Once the butterknife is clean, going to the drawer is correct, and a model that simply follows the words of the task gets it right. We therefore fix such a surface shortcut for each domain.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，知道某个决策依赖于模拟，并不能将真正的成功与幸运的猜测区分开来。 当表面的捷径恰好指向正确的候选选项时，模型就能做出正确的决策。 考虑这样一个任务：“把一把干净的餐刀放进抽屉里”。 一旦餐刀干净了，去拿抽屉里的东西就是正确的做法，而一个仅仅遵循任务描述的模型也能正确完成这个任务。 因此，我们为每个领域都修正了这类表面的捷径。

sents.en: Knowing that a decision depends on simulation, however, does not separate real success from a lucky guess.
sents.zh: 然而，知道某个决策依赖于模拟，并不能将真正的成功与幸运的猜测区分开来。

sents.en: A model can get such a decision right when a surface shortcut happens to point to the correct candidate option.
sents.zh: 当表面的捷径恰好指向正确的候选选项时，模型就能做出正确的决策。

sents.en: Consider the task “put a clean butterknife in drawer”.
sents.zh: 考虑这样一个任务：“把一把干净的餐刀放进抽屉里”。

sents.en: Once the butterknife is clean, going to the drawer is correct, and a model that simply follows the words of the task gets it right.
sents.zh: 一旦餐刀干净了，去拿抽屉里的东西就是正确的做法，而一个仅仅遵循任务描述的模型也能正确完成这个任务。

sents.en: We therefore fix such a surface shortcut for each domain.
sents.zh: 因此，我们为每个领域都修正了这类表面的捷径。

paragraphs.en: For each domain, the surface shortcut h h is a simple rule, fixed in advance, that picks the candidate options that look most relevant from the input alone, without predicting anything. A decision that depends on simulation is aligned if h h picks a correct candidate option and misleading otherwise. In a misleading decision, the candidate options that h h picks are the lure .
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个领域，表面捷径 h h 是一条预先固定的简单规则，它仅根据输入选择看起来最相关的候选选项，而无需进行任何预测。 如果 h h 选择了正确的候选选项，则依赖于模拟的决策是合理的；否则则是误导性的。 在误导性决策中，h h 所选择的候选选项就是诱饵。

sents.en: For each domain, the surface shortcut h h is a simple rule, fixed in advance, that picks the candidate options that look most relevant from the input alone, without predicting anything.
sents.zh: 对于每个领域，表面捷径 h h 是一条预先固定的简单规则，它仅根据输入选择看起来最相关的候选选项，而无需进行任何预测。

sents.en: A decision that depends on simulation is aligned if h h picks a correct candidate option and misleading otherwise.
sents.zh: 如果 h h 选择了正确的候选选项，则依赖于模拟的决策是合理的；否则则是误导性的。

sents.en: In a misleading decision, the candidate options that h h picks are the lure .
sents.zh: 在误导性决策中，h h 所选择的候选选项就是诱饵。

paragraphs.en: In games, h h picks the action with the highest average payoff, as if the opponent acted at random. This is the level-1 rule of behavioral game theory ( Stahl and Wilson, 1995 ; Costa-Gomes et al., 2001 ) . In ALFWorld, h h picks the commands that mention an object or place named in the task description. Following Hagendorff et al. (2023) , we classify each answer to a misleading decision as correct , lure or other . If most errors are caused by lures, the model is being drawn to the surface shortcut. If errors are spread over the other wrong options, they are more likely random noise.
paragraphs.zh: 在游戏中，h h 会选择平均收益最高的行动，仿佛对手是随机行动的。这是行为博弈论中的第 1 级规则（Stahl and Wilson, 1995；Costa-Gomes et al., 2001）。在 ALFWorld 中，h h 会选择任务描述中提及的物体或地点相关的命令。遵循 Hagendorff et al. (2023) 的做法，我们将误导性决策中的每个答案分为“正确”“诱饵”或“其他”。如果大多数错误是由“诱饵”引起的，说明模型被表面捷径所吸引。如果错误分散在其他错误选项中，则更可能是随机噪声。

paragraphs.en: Predictions. Our claim concerns what Jev does, not how it works internally. If Jev evaluates but does not simulate, five things should hold. (i) Decisions that need only evaluation are answered well, even against an intuitive but wrong option. (ii) Aligned decisions that depend on simulation are answered well, because the surface shortcut picks a correct candidate option. (iii) Misleading decisions that depend on simulation fail, and the errors go to the lure. (iv) Stating the missing prediction z z in the input, such as the opponent’s action, restores accuracy. (v) If Jev can predict z z in a separate call, writing its answer back also restores accuracy. Prediction (v) tells whether Jev cannot predict z z at all, or can predict it correctly when asked separately but fails when it must also make the choice in the same call. By contrast, if intuitive lures were enough to mislead Jev, it would fail the CRT, whose questions are built around intuitive but wrong answers. If Jev simply lacked reasoning, it would also fail when asked to predict the opponent’s action on its own.
paragraphs.zh: 预测。 我们的主张涉及 Jev 做了什么，而非其内部运作方式。 如果 Jev 仅进行评估而不进行模拟，则以下五点应成立。 (i) 仅需评估的决策能得到正确回答，即使面对一个看似直观但错误的选项也是如此。 (ii) 依赖模拟的对齐决策能得到正确回答，因为表层捷径会选择一个正确的候选选项。 (iii) 依赖模拟的误导性决策则会失败，且错误会导向诱饵。 (iv) 在输入中说明缺失的预测 z z（例如对手的行动），即可恢复准确性。 (v) 如果 Jev 能在单独调用中预测 z z，将其答案写回同样能恢复准确性。 预测 (v) 表明 Jev 是完全无法预测 z z，还是在单独被问及时能正确预测，但在同一调用中必须同时做出选择时却会失败。 相比之下，如果仅凭直观的诱饵就足以误导 Jev，那么它将无法通过 CRT，因为 CRT 的问题正是围绕直观但错误的答案构建的。 如果 Jev 仅仅缺乏推理能力，那么在单独被要求预测对手行动时也会失败。

paragraphs.en: Protocol. The order of the candidate options shifts Jev’s probabilities, so we average each decision over several orders. Whether a decision needs only evaluation or depends on simulation, and whether it is aligned or misleading, are computed from the environment, never from Jev’s choices.
paragraphs.zh: 协议。 候选选项的顺序会改变 Jev 的概率，因此我们对每个决策在多种顺序下取平均值。 一项决策是仅需评估还是依赖模拟，以及它是正确的还是误导性的，这些都由环境计算得出，绝不会由 Jev 的选择决定。

sents.zh: 协议。

sents.en: The order of the candidate options shifts Jev’s probabilities, so we average each decision over several orders.

paragraphs.en: Results. Jev picks the correct answer on 99% of questions and the intuitive answer on 1% (Table 1 ). For reference, people answering the same questions in open form give the intuitive answer 55% of the time. Each question also has a control version without the trap, in which the intuitive answer is correct. Jev is right on 96% of these, so it does not simply avoid intuitive-looking options. Because the answers are listed as options, Jev only needs to check each one against the conditions in the question (Example 3 ). Such checking needs only evaluation, so prediction (i) holds: an intuitive lure alone does not make Jev fail. Next, we further validate this boundary on one-shot matrix games, where the right action can depend on a prediction of the opponent’s action.

paragraphs.en: Setup. We sample random 3 × 3 3{\times}3 matrix games with distinct payoffs in 0–99 that iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies solves to a unique outcome. Jev plays Row against a Column described as rational and informed. The depth D D is the number of elimination rounds Row needs, minus one, so D = 0 D{=}0 means Row has a dominant action, one that pays more than every other action whatever Column plays. At D = k D{=}k , Row must reason k k steps about Column, such as “Column will never play this action, so I should play that one”. A game is aligned if Row’s best action against a rational Column, the equilibrium action, is also the action with the highest average payoff, and misleading otherwise. We sample 30 games for each value of depth and alignment, resulting in 210 games in total. Each game is shown with Row’s three actions in three different orders. We compare three conditions. In the plain condition, Jev sees only the payoff table. In the reason condition, the instruction also tells Jev to first rule out the actions that Column would never play. In the told condition, code adds Column’s equilibrium action to the state, as in “Column will play Y.”, which tests prediction (iv) .
paragraphs.zh: 设置。 我们采样生成随机 3 × 3 矩阵博弈，其中各支付值在 0–99 范围内且互不相同，通过严格占优策略的迭代剔除可得出唯一结果。 Jev 扮演行方，与一个被描述为理性且知情的列方进行博弈。 深度 D 是行方所需的剔除轮数减一，因此 D = 0 表示行方存在一个占优行动，无论列方采取何种行动，该行动的支付值都高于其他所有行动。 在 D = k 时，行方必须对列方的行为进行 k 步推理，例如：“列方绝不会采取这个行动，因此我应该采取那个行动”。 如果行方面对理性列方时的最佳行动（即均衡行动）同时也是平均支付值最高的行动，则该博弈是“对齐”的；否则即为“误导性”的。 我们对每种深度和对齐状态采样 30 个博弈，总共得到 210 个博弈。 每个博弈都会显示行方的三个行动，但顺序各不相同。 我们比较三种条件。 在“普通”条件下，Jev 只能看到支付表。 在“推理”条件下，说明还要求 Jev 首先排除列方绝不会采取的行动。 在“告知”条件下，代码会将列方的均衡行动加入状态信息中，例如“列方将采取 Y”，以此检验预测 (iv)。

paragraphs.en: Results. Figure 2 shows that alignment, not depth, determines accuracy. With a dominant action, which is best whatever Column plays and so needs only evaluation, Jev is perfect. In aligned games it stays at 77–93% for every depth. In misleading games it falls to chance (28–37%) and picks the lure in 53–71% of games. A regression confirms that depth has no detectable effect once alignment is taken into account (Appendix C ). An instruction to reason leaves misleading games at chance, whereas stating Column’s action lifts them to 97–99%. This confirms predictions (i)–(iv) .
paragraphs.zh: 结果。 图 2 显示，决定准确性的是对齐而非深度。 对于主导行动而言，无论 Column 采取何种策略，它都是最佳选择，因此只需进行评估，Jev 的表现即完美无缺。 在对齐游戏中，其准确率在每个深度下都保持在 77%–93%。 在误导性游戏中，准确率则降至随机水平（28%–37%），且有 53%–71% 的游戏中会选择诱饵。 回归分析证实，一旦考虑对齐因素，深度便不再产生可检测的影响（附录 C）。 若仅指示进行推理，误导性游戏的准确率将保持在随机水平；而明确说明 Column 的行动，则可将准确率提升至 97%–99%。 这证实了预测 (i)–(iv)。

paragraphs.en: Which rule produces these choices? A one-parameter softmax over each action’s average payoff, a soft version of the surface shortcut, fits Jev’s probabilities best (Appendix C ). Adding whether an action is the equilibrium barely improves the fit. Jev thus plays as if its rational opponent acted at random, a quantal level-1 player in the terms of behavioral game theory ( McKelvey and Palfrey, 1995 ; Stahl and Wilson, 1995 ) . Level 1 involves no reasoning about the opponent, so it is not the same as depth D = 1 D{=}1 .
paragraphs.zh: 是哪条规则产生了这些选择？ 对每个行动的预期收益采用单参数 softmax 函数（即表面捷径的软化版本），能最好地拟合 Jev 的概率分布（附录 C）。 加入某个行动是否为均衡状态这一因素，几乎无法改善拟合效果。 因此，Jev 的行为就好像其理性对手是随机行动的——用行为博弈论的术语来说，就是一个量子水平 1 的玩家（McKelvey and Palfrey, 1995；Stahl and Wilson, 1995）。 水平 1 不涉及对对手的推理，因此它与深度 D = 1 的情况并不相同。

paragraphs.en: Does Jev fail because it cannot predict Column’s action, or because it cannot use that prediction while choosing? Following Hagendorff et al. (2023) , we ask for the prediction in a separate call on the same games. Jev correctly predicts Column’s equilibrium action 90% of the time, mostly by picking the column that pays Column the most on average. Yet Jev’s own choice does not use this prediction. In the plain condition, Jev chooses correctly in 32% of the calls with a right prediction and in 35% of the calls with a wrong prediction. A choice that used the prediction would be right in almost all calls with a right prediction, as in the told condition (98%). Jev thus fails when one call must both perform the simulation and evaluate based on it.
paragraphs.zh: Jev 的失败，是因为它无法预测 Column 的行为，还是因为它在做出选择时无法利用这一预测？遵循 Hagendorff 等人（2023）的研究方法，我们在同一组游戏中通过一次独立的调用来获取预测结果。Jev 有 90% 的概率正确预测出 Column 的均衡行为，这主要得益于它选择了平均而言能为 Column 带来最高回报的列。然而，Jev 自身的选择并未利用这一预测。在普通条件下，当预测正确时，Jev 有 32% 的调用做出了正确的选择；而当预测错误时，这一比例为 35%。如果选择过程能够利用预测结果，那么在预测正确的几乎所有调用中，选择都会是正确的，就像在“告知”条件下那样（98%）。因此，当一次调用必须同时执行模拟并基于模拟结果进行评价时，Jev 就会失败。

paragraphs.en: Separating simulation and evaluation recovers the decision. Code first asks Jev to predict Column’s action and then writes the answer into the state, as in the told condition. Accuracy in misleading games rises from 33% to 94%, as prediction (v) expects. The gain follows the written content. When Jev’s own prediction is wrong, code writes a wrong action into the state, and Jev still plays the best response to that written action in 24 of 26 calls.

paragraphs.en: Setup. To test single decisions, we replay the successful trajectories from ALFWorld’s hand-coded expert. At each step Jev sees the task, the observation, the full history and the admissible commands. A choice is correct if it lies in an acceptable set derived from the environment. For example, when the expert goes to sinkbasin 1 to wash the knife, going to sinkbasin 2 also counts as correct. We label each step with one of four types that we define in advance and compute automatically from the task and the history (Appendix D ). E steps directly complete part of the task, such as taking the butterknife, cleaning it or putting it in the drawer. Whether such a command is right can be read from the command itself, so these steps need only evaluation. S-known steps complete no part of the task themselves but make a later step possible, such as going to the sink while holding an unwashed butterknife. They depend on simulation, although all information needed for them is in the history. S-search steps explore for an object not yet seen, so the needed information is missing from both the history and the current state. Therefore, they also depend on simulation. Other steps, mostly looking around or closing a receptacle, neither complete part of the task nor make a later step possible. We exclude them (22% of expert steps). We test on both of ALFWorld’s evaluation splits, called seen and unseen. The 140 seen games take place in rooms that also appear in ALFWorld’s training data, and the 134 unseen games take place in new rooms. We use Jev zero-shot on both. The surface shortcut splits S steps into aligned and misleading (Section 2 ). We defined the ALFWorld surface shortcut according to the unseen games, such as picking “go to drawer 1” for the task “put a clean butterknife in drawer”, and then tested it on the seen games (Appendix D ).

paragraphs.en: Results. Figure 3 a follows one seen game. Jev gets the E steps right, such as taking and cleaning the butterknife. paragraphs.en: Does Jev lack the order of subgoals, or fail to use it? ALFWorld writes each task in one of two forms, the ordered form and the goal form (Example 5.2 ). Asked separately for the next subgoal, Jev answers correctly 100% of the time under the ordered form but only 33% under the goal form. Under the ordered form, Jev thus knows the next subgoal, yet its decisions made in a single call are right only 68% of the time. Writing its own answer into the input raises them to 86%, as prediction (v) expects (Table 2 ). Under the goal form, Jev’s own prediction is wrong 67% of the time, and its wrong answers always skip to putting the object in place. The order of subgoals must therefore come from code, in one of two ways. Code can add the correct next subgoal to the input, which raises decisions to 92%. Code can also rewrite the task into the ordered form, which raises them from 6% to 73% over both seen and unseen games (Appendix F ).
paragraphs.zh: Jev 是缺少子目标顺序，还是未能利用它？ ALFWorld 以两种形式之一编写每个任务：有序形式和目标形式（示例 5.2）。 当单独询问下一个子目标时，在有序形式下 Jev 的回答正确率是 100%，而在目标形式下仅为 33%。 因此，在有序形式下，Jev 知道下一个子目标，但它在单次调用中做出的决策正确率仅为 68%。 将其自身答案写入输入后，正确率提升至 86%，正如预测 (v) 所预期的那样（表 2）。 在目标形式下，Jev 自身的预测有 67% 的时间是错误的，且其错误答案总是直接跳过步骤，将物体放置到位。 因此，子目标的顺序必须来自代码，并且有两种实现方式之一。 代码可以将正确的下一个子目标添加到输入中，这将决策正确率提升至 92%。 代码也可以将任务重写为有序形式，这使得在已见和未见游戏中，正确率从 6% 提升至 73%（附录 F）。

paragraphs.en: Does the same division hold in robot control? Here the missing prediction is the physics. Whether a torque is good depends on how the arm will move next, and the state describes only where the arm is now. We therefore expect Jev to fail when it chooses raw torques. In contrast, we expect it to succeed when code performs the physics simulation and Jev only chooses among described outcomes. We test both cases on the same task, Stacker from the DeepMind Control Suite ( Tassa et al., 2018 ) , where a planar arm with a two-finger gripper must bring a box to a target marker, a red square that shows where the box should go, either on the floor or one box above it.
paragraphs.zh: 同样的划分在机器人控制中是否也成立？ 在这里，缺失的预测是物理规律。 一个力矩是否合适取决于机械臂接下来将如何移动，而状态仅描述了机械臂当前的位置。 因此，我们预计当 Jev 选择原始力矩时会失败。 相比之下，当代码执行物理模拟且 Jev 仅在已描述的结果中进行选择时，我们预计它会成功。 我们在同一任务上测试这两种情况，即来自 DeepMind Control Suite（Tassa et al., 2018）的 Stacker 任务，其中带有双指夹爪的平面机械臂必须将一个盒子移动到目标标记处——一个显示盒子应放置位置的红色方块，该位置可能在地板上，也可能在盒子正上方。

As a result, every skill corresponds to a physics simulation implemented by code. In other words, when Jev reads the skill options, it knows the outcome of that simulation. paragraphs.en: Generalization to new instructions. To test generalization, we extend the native task with five new instructions, such as “put box0 on box1” or “move the farther box to the target”, each run on 8 seeds with different starting conditions. We change the instruction text, while the skills are shared. Jev solves 22 of the 40 episodes, against 3 for the hand-written controller and none for random choice. We find that Jev’s evaluation ability, with skills developed for one task, provides promising generalization to unseen task variants. Figure 4 shows one such episode. Although the settings with and without physics simulation differ in the action level, their contrast shows that code provides the simulation, so that Jev only needs to evaluate.

paragraphs.en: Language models as policies over candidate actions. A common way to use a language model as an agent is to let code list valid actions and let the model score them, as in SayCan ( Ahn et al., 2022 ) and admissible-action mapping ( Huang et al., 2022 ) . Text-game agents choose among TextWorld and ALFWorld commands ( Côté et al., 2018 ; Shridhar et al., 2021 ) , with or without reasoning traces ( Yao et al., 2023b ; Shinn et al., 2023 ) . GLAM and TWOSOME train such scorers with RL ( Carta et al., 2023 ; Tan et al., 2024 ) , and TALES collects text-adventure benchmarks ( Cui et al., 2025 ) . These works report how often an agent succeeds. We instead ask which decisions such a scorer gets right. The answer depends on whether a decision needs only evaluation or depends on simulation, which we determine from the environment, not from the model.

paragraphs.en: Cognitive and strategic probes. The CRT is built so that the intuitive answer is wrong ( Frederick, 2005 ) . Hagendorff et al. (2023) found that earlier GPT-3 models fall for it while ChatGPT-4 does not, and we borrow their error scoring and direct knowledge probes. Other work applies cognitive tasks to language models ( Binz and Schulz, 2023 ; Coda-Forno et al., 2024 ) , and HANS splits items by whether a known heuristic answers them ( McCoy et al., 2019 ) , which our aligned/misleading split mirrors. Behavioral game theory describes players by their depth of reasoning about others ( Nagel, 1995 ; Stahl and Wilson, 1995 ; Camerer et al., 2004 ; Costa-Gomes et al., 2001 ) , and human play departs from equilibrium in systematic ways ( Goeree and Holt, 2001 ; Arad and Rubinstein, 2012 ) . We vary depth and surface alignment separately and add a condition in which code states the opponent’s action.
paragraphs.zh: 认知与策略性探测。CRT 的设计使得直觉性答案是错误的（Frederick，2005）。Hagendorff 等人（2023）发现，早期的 GPT-3 模型会陷入这一陷阱，而 ChatGPT-4 则不会；我们借鉴了他们的错误评分和直接知识探测方法。其他研究也将认知任务应用于语言模型（Binz 和 Schulz，2023；Coda-Forno 等人，2024），而 HANS 则根据问题能否通过已知的启发式方法回答来对题目进行分类（McCoy 等人，2019），这与我们的“对齐/误导性”分类方式相一致。行为博弈论通过玩家对他人的推理深度来描述其策略（Nagel，1995；Stahl 和 Wilson，1995；Camerer 等人，2004；Costa-Gomes 等人，2001），而人类的实际博弈行为也会以系统化的方式偏离均衡状态（Goeree 和 Holt，2001；Arad 和 Rubinstein，2012）。我们分别调整推理深度和表面对齐程度，并增加了一个通过代码明确说明对手行动的条件。

paragraphs.en: The boundary lies inside a single call. Across the four settings, Jev succeeds at evaluation when the input contains sufficient information. It fails when the right option depends on simulation to provide information missing from the input. When it fails, it picks the lure. In misleading matrix games, 90% of its errors go to the action with the highest average payoff, against 50% expected under random errors. At misleading ALFWorld steps, 89% go to a command that mentions the task, against 12% expected (Figure 6 in the appendix). In robot control, it never picks up a box when it must choose raw torques. Table 2 shows which part fails. Asked in a separate call, Jev predicts Column’s action correctly in 90% of misleading games. When code writes a correct prediction into the input, Jev chooses correctly in 98% of them. It fails when one call must both perform the simulation and evaluate based on it, where it is right in only 33%. This also explains why an instruction to reason does not help, since the instruction adds no prediction. Two limits remain. First, some facts are relations between options, such as one action paying more than another whatever the opponent does. Such a fact cannot be read from any single option. Jev mostly misses it, even when asked in a separate call, so code must compute it (Appendix F ). Second, Jev follows the order in which the task mentions the actions, even when a word such as “after” says otherwise (Example 8 ).

paragraphs.en: When can code make the prediction or simulation? In RL terms, code supplies the world model that Jev lacks. With a simulator, such as the game rules, a copy of the game or a physics engine, code can compute the prediction directly. Jev then only evaluates. This works when Jev can make the prediction from the input. When Jev lacks the ability to simulate a given environment, as with the unwashed knife, the prediction must come from elsewhere, for example a learned world model ( Ha and Schmidhuber, 2018 ; Hafner et al., 2020 ) or a larger reasoning model.

paragraphs.en: Limitations. We study one model and one API version. We have not tested other models that answer without reasoning text, nor how the boundary moves when reasoning is allowed. paragraphs.en: We began with a contrast. Jev solves the counterintuitive CRT questions, yet it carries an unwashed butterknife to the drawer instead of the sinkbasin. The two lures differ in where the answer lies. A CRT answer can be checked against the question, which is evaluation. The sinkbasin is right only because the knife must be washed first, which the input does not describe and Jev must simulate. Jev evaluates well, and in games it can often predict the opponent’s action when asked separately. It fails when one call must both perform the simulation and evaluate based on it. Letting code make the prediction or simulation closes this gap. Code can state the opponent’s action, write back Jev’s own prediction, show the outcome of each command, or simulate each skill of a robot arm. With these simulations, Jev becomes an expert controller through its general evaluation ability, and in robot control it follows new instructions that a hand-written controller cannot. Code should own the simulation, and Jev the evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 我们从对比开始。 Jev 能够解决那些反直觉的 CRT 问题，但它却把一把未清洗的餐刀放进抽屉，而不是水槽。 这两种诱饵的不同之处在于答案的位置。 CRT 的答案可以与问题对照检查，这就是评估。 水槽之所以正确，仅仅是因为这把刀必须先清洗，而输入并未说明这一点，Jev 必须自行模拟。 Jev 的评估能力很强，在游戏当中，当被单独询问时，它通常能预测对手的行动。 当一个调用必须同时执行模拟并基于此进行评估时，它便会失败。 让代码负责预测或模拟，就能填补这一差距。 代码可以陈述对手的行动、回写 Jev 自己的预测、展示每条命令的结果，或者模拟机器人手臂的每一项技能。 借助这些模拟，Jev 凭借其通用的评估能力成为了一名专家控制器，在机器人控制中，它能执行手写控制器无法完成的新指令。 模拟应由代码负责，而评估则由 Jev 负责。

sents.en: We began with a contrast.

sents.en: Jev solves the counterintuitive CRT questions, yet it carries an unwashed butterknife to the drawer instead of the sinkbasin.
sents.zh: Jev 能够解决那些反直觉的 CRT 问题，但它却把一把未清洗的餐刀放进抽屉，而不是水槽。

sents.en: The two lures differ in where the answer lies.
sents.zh: 这两种诱饵的不同之处在于答案的位置。

sents.en: A CRT answer can be checked against the question, which is evaluation.
sents.zh: CRT 的答案可以与问题对照检查，这就是评估。

sents.en: The sinkbasin is right only because the knife must be washed first, which the input does not describe and Jev must simulate.
sents.zh: 水槽之所以正确，仅仅是因为这把刀必须先清洗，而输入并未说明这一点，Jev 必须自行模拟。

sents.en: Jev evaluates well, and in games it can often predict the opponent’s action when asked separately.
sents.zh: Jev 的评估能力很强，在游戏当中，当被单独询问时，它通常能预测对手的行动。

sents.en: Letting code make the prediction or simulation closes this gap.
sents.zh: 让代码负责预测或模拟，就能填补这一差距。

sents.zh: 代码可以陈述对手的行动、回写 Jev 自己的预测、展示每条命令的结果，或者模拟机器人手臂的每一项技能。

sents.en: Code should own the simulation, and Jev the evaluation.

paragraphs.en: Every call is one request to the TypeSafe System One API with the model jev-1.13.0 ( TypeSafe, 2026 ) . A request carries a JSON state and one choice question. paragraphs.en: Stacker with raw torques. State rules : A planar arm in the x-z plane with a root, shoulder, elbow and wrist joint and a two-finger gripper. Commands are normalized torques, not position targets. Gravity pulls the arm down, so a zero command lets it sag, and holding a pose needs a steady torque. Options One question for each actuator (root, shoulder, elbow, wrist, grasp). Five torque levels: strong_positive , gentle_positive , none , gentle_negative , strong_negative . For example, strong_negative for the elbow reads “Maximum torque that lowers the elbow angle, so the hand moves right (+x) and slightly up”. paragraphs.en: We use the 150 questions of Hagendorff et al. (2023) (OSF w5vhp ), 50 of each type. Type 1 follows the bat and ball, as in “A pear and a fridge together cost $140. paragraphs.en: Our first run reached 88% on the control versions. The errors came from two ambiguities. First, a type-2 control asks “How long does it take 7 people to tailor 4 jackets, if it takes 7 people 7 hours to tailor 7 jackets?”. The intended answer is 4 hours, but 7 hours is also right if each person makes a whole jacket. Second, the sentence we appended to type-3 controls to state a constant rate did not fit every story. A falling branch, for example, does not “grow”. The reported run fixes both. It appends “They share the work evenly, so any job can be split among all of them.” to both versions of type-2 questions. This sentence does not change the answer of the lure version. It appends “Assume it progresses at a constant rate, so equal amounts are added in equal periods of time.” to type-3 controls. Controls then rose to 96%, with type 2 going from 78% to 92% and type 3 from 85% to 96%. Most remaining control errors are type-2 questions such as asking how long 8 painters take to paint 1 painting when 8 painters paint 8 paintings in 8 hours. The intended answer is 1 hour, but splitting one painting among eight painters conflicts with common sense. The revision does not affect the main result. In both runs, Jev answers 99% of the lure questions correctly.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的第一次运行在控制版本中达到了 88%。 这些错误源于两个模糊之处。 首先，一种类型 2 的控制问题会问：“如果 7 个人需要 7 小时才能缝制 7 件夹克，那么 7 个人缝制 4 件夹克需要多长时间？” 预期的答案是 4 小时，但如果每个人都能独立完成一件夹克，那么 7 小时也是正确的。 其次，我们附加在类型 3 控制问题中以说明恒定速率的句子并不适用于所有情境。 例如，一根掉落的树枝并不会“生长”。 报告中的这次运行解决了这两个问题。 它在类型 2 问题的两个版本中都附加了这句话：“他们平均分配工作，因此任何任务都可以由他们所有人共同完成。” 这句话不会改变诱饵版本的答案。 它在类型 3 的控制问题中附加了这句话：“假设它以恒定速率进行，因此在相等的时间内会增加相等的量。” 随后，控制问题的正确率上升到了 96%，其中类型 2 从 78% 提升至 92%，类型 3 从 85% 提升至 96%。 大多数剩余的控制问题错误都来自类型 2 的问题，例如：当 8 个油漆工在 8 小时内完成 8 幅画作时，他们画完 1 幅画需要多长时间。 预期的答案是 1 小时，但将一幅画分配给八位油漆工的做法与常识相悖。 这次修订并未影响主要结果。 在两次运行中，Jev 都正确回答了 99% 的诱饵问题。

paragraphs.en: Step types. The type depends on the expert’s command and the tracked state. A step is E if the command changes a goal fact: taking the object, cleaning, heating or cooling it, putting it in the destination, or using the desk lamp while holding the object. A step is S-known if the command changes no goal fact but goes to or opens a receptacle that a later goal step needs, such as the sink while holding an unwashed object, or returns to where the object was seen. A step is S-search if the needed object has not been seen yet and the command goes to or opens a receptacle to look for it. All other steps, such as looking around, closing a receptacle or discarding a wrong object, are labeled other and excluded.
paragraphs.zh: 步骤类型。 类型取决于专家的指令和所跟踪的状态。 如果指令改变了某个目标事实，则此步骤为 E：例如拿起物体、清洁它、加热或冷却它、将其放入目的地，或在手持物体的同时使用台灯。 如果指令未改变任何目标事实，但前往或打开了后续目标步骤所需的容器（例如在手持未清洗的物体时走向水槽），或返回到曾看到物体的位置，则此步骤为 S-known。 如果所需物体尚未被看到，且指令是前往或打开容器以寻找该物体，则此步骤为 S-search。 所有其他步骤（例如环顾四周、关闭容器或丢弃错误物体）均标记为 other 并被排除在外。

paragraphs.en: Lookahead. ALFWorld keeps its game state inside a C library, so the game cannot be copied from Python. At each decision, the process holding the game forks once per admissible command. Each child runs its command, sends back the game’s output, the new admissible commands and the win flag, and exits, so the parent’s game is left untouched. A random policy with a fixed seed produces identical trajectories with and without lookahead, so the lookahead does not change the game. The predicted outputs also match the real ones at every step. Per decision, the forked lookahead took about 3 s and the Jev call about 0.4 s. Table 6 gives the closed-loop results. Lookahead v1 solves 41 games that Jev alone fails and fails 4 that it solves (exact McNemar test, p = 9 × 10 − 9 p=9\times 10^{-9} ). Lookahead v2 gains 38 games over v1 and loses 1 ( p = 1.5 × 10 − 10 p=1.5\times 10^{-10} ). The word-overlap rule uses no model. It scores each option, the command together with its predicted output, by the words it shares with the task and picks the best option whose output was not already seen.

paragraphs.en: Game questions. The probes use the 180 games with D ≥ 1 D\geq 1 , each in three orders of Row’s actions, with the state of the plain condition. The prediction question asks “Which action will Column play?”. Its options describe Column’s payoffs for each of its actions. An elimination question asks which of one player’s remaining actions is strictly dominated, that is, pays less than another remaining action of the same player against every remaining action of the other player. Its options are the remaining actions and “none”. In the elimination write-back, code asks Column and Row in turn and writes each answer into the state as a note, such as “Column will never play Z.”. paragraphs.en: Game results. When Column had a dominated action, Jev named it in 19% of steps and wrongly answered “none” in 81%. When Column had none, it answered correctly in 98%. For Row, the same two accuracies were 58% and 85%. Overall, single elimination steps are correct in 57% of calls. With correct elimination notes, decisions in misleading games reach 94%, but with Jev’s own elimination steps written back they reach only 43%. In the prediction probe, Jev picks the column with the highest average payoff to Column in 88% of calls. paragraphs.en: ALFWorld results. At the 149 aligned S-known steps, where the next subgoal is to put the object, predicting the subgoal, deciding with the correct subgoal given and deciding with Jev’s own subgoal written back all reach 100%. At misleading steps, Jev names the subgoal correctly in 63% of calls, and every error names putting the object. By task type, it is right in 77% of clean, 57% of heat and 50% of cool steps. With the correct subgoal given, clean and heat steps reach 100% and cool steps 70%. On cool steps Jev then often goes to the sink or to the destination. Table 2 uses the 64 misleading seen-split steps at which the object must still be cleaned, heated or cooled, 28 in the ordered form and 36 in the goal form, each in two option orders. The other 6 misleading steps belong to lamp and two-object tasks, which have neither form. The game row of Table 2 uses the 90 misleading games in three orders.

paragraphs.en: Task wording. ALFWorld writes each clean, heat or cool task in the ordered form or the goal form (Example 5.2 ), using fixed templates such as “heat some T and put it in D.” and “put a hot T in D.”, where T is the object and D the destination. Code swaps only the template. This moves decisions from 6% to 73% when the goal form becomes the ordered form, and from 66% to 11% the other way, and the subgoal answers flip with them (Figure 5 ). A third template, “put some T in D after cleaning it”, says with “after” that cleaning comes first but mentions putting first. With it, decisions reach only 24% (Example 8 ).
paragraphs.zh: 任务描述。 ALFWorld 将每个清洁、加热或冷却任务以有序形式或目标形式（示例 5.2）书写，并使用固定模板，例如“加热某个 T 并将其放入 D”和“将热的 T 放入 D”，其中 T 是物体，D 是目的地。 代码仅替换模板。 当目标形式变为有序形式时，这会将决策比例从 6% 提升至 73%，而反向变化时则从 66% 降至 11%，子目标答案也随之翻转（图 5）。 第三个模板是“在清洁某个 T 后将其放入 D”，通过“之后”一词表明清洁应先进行，但首先提到了放置动作。 使用此模板时，决策比例仅达到 24%（示例 8）。

paragraphs.en: Figure 6 scores every decision that has a lure as correct, as the lure, or as another error ( Hagendorff et al., 2023 ) . If Jev’s errors were spread evenly over the wrong options, the lure would receive one in three errors in the CRT, one in two in games and about one in eight in ALFWorld. Instead, almost all errors go to the lure. In the CRT, the few errors (1%) all pick the intuitive answer. In misleading games, 90% of errors pick the action with the highest average payoff. At misleading S-known ALFWorld steps, 89% pick a command that mentions the task. When code supplies the missing prediction, most decisions move from the lure to the correct option. Stating Column’s action leaves 2% errors in games, and the lookahead cuts the lure rate in ALFWorld from 56% to 21%.
paragraphs.zh: 图 6 将每个包含诱饵项的决策都判定为正确，无论是选择诱饵项还是其他错误选项（Hagendorff 等，2023）。 如果 Jev 的错误均匀分布在错误选项中，那么在 CRT 中诱饵项会承担三分之一的错误，在游戏里占二分之一，在 ALFWorld 中则约为八分之一。 实际上，几乎所有错误都集中在诱饵项上。 在 CRT 中，少数错误（1%）全部选择了直觉性答案。 在具有误导性的游戏中，90% 的错误选择了平均收益最高的行动。 在具有误导性的 S-known ALFWorld 步骤中，89% 的错误选择了提及任务的命令。 当代码提供缺失的预测时，大多数决策会从诱饵项转向正确选项。 明确说明 Column 的行动后，游戏中的错误率降至 2%，而前瞻机制则将 ALFWorld 中的诱饵项选择率从 56% 降低到了 21%。
